newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's new pension funds seen managing $24 bln.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's new pension funds seen managing $24 bln.

text.p: Mexico's AFORES, or private retirement funds, could manage US$24 billion or 6.6 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) by the end of the century, Salomon Brothers said in a report.
The company said the amount of assets under management will reach close to 20 percent of GDP in 15 years.
"Based on our models, the AFORES will receive an average of $3.7 billion per year over the next ten years, 20 percent of which will be invested in the equity market," Salomon Brothers said.
The company said that the "private pension fund effect" on the stock market will result in a real advance of 7.5 percent over the next 15 years in equities.
It said that the private pension fund system in Mexico will not break even until 2001, and that consolidation of the 20 initial companies will start soon.
"After a few months, we estimate that 14 groups will be fighting for 20 percent market share," it said.

Salomon Brothers said that the future decision of initial market shares allocated to the Administrators of Retirement Funds (AFORES) will be the most important issue facing the new social security system, as it will determine its form and competition.
The AFORES were originally scheduled to come into effect on January 1, but the start-up date has been delayed to mid-1997.
